security_audit.summary: All 51 static matches are false positives: Markdown formatting, example URLs, and legitimate browser operations do not establish the reported threats. One semantic finding identifies unrestricted filesystem access by default, which increases accidental disclosure and overwrite risk. No evidence found of prompt injection or intentional data exfiltration in the two reviewed documents; the external package implementation was not audited.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted filesystem access is the documented default for file saving and uploads.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend --allowUnrestrictedPaths=false during setup and store artifacts in the OS temporary directory. Require explicit approval for broader paths and each file upload.

content.user_title: Automate and Debug Chrome from the Command Line
content.value_statement: Manual browser testing makes repeated interactions and debugging time consuming. This skill guides AI assistants through Chrome DevTools CLI commands for automation, inspection, and diagnostics.
actual_capabilities: Navigate browser pages and automate clicks, text entry, dialogs, and file uploads using snapshot element identifiers.
Inspect accessibility snapshots, console messages, CSS styles, and captured network requests.
Capture screenshots, run Lighthouse audits, and record performance traces.
Capture heap snapshots and inspect memory details when memory debugging is enabled.
Emulate network conditions, CPU throttling, viewport sizes, geolocation, and color schemes.
Manage browser extensions and use PWA or experimental tools when their required feature flags are enabled.
limitations: Requires a separate chrome-devtools-mcp installation and a working browser environment.
Provides command guidance rather than a standalone test suite or browser engine.
Memory debugging, PWA tools, and experimental tools require explicit flags; screencast recording also requires ffmpeg.
Filesystem access is unrestricted by default; restricted mode limits file access to the OS temporary directory.

use_cases.title: Reproduce Interface Defects
use_cases.description: Repeat page interactions, inspect console errors, and capture screenshots to document a frontend defect.

use_cases.title: Check Browser Workflows
use_cases.description: Exercise navigation, forms, and dialogs on a test site, then report observed behavior and failed steps.

use_cases.title: Investigate Runtime Performance
use_cases.description: Record performance traces, inspect request activity, and compare heap snapshots to investigate slow pages or memory growth.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an Open Page
prompt_templates.prompt: List open browser pages and inspect the page titled [title]. Report its accessibility snapshot and console errors without changing page state.

prompt_templates.title: Exercise a Test Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [test URL], inspect the form, and enter [test values]. Ask before submitting, then report the resulting page state.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Responsive Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [test URL] at desktop and mobile viewport sizes. Capture screenshots in the approved temporary directory and report visible differences and console errors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: viewport emulation and evidence collection

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Slow Interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: On [test URL], trace [interaction] and inspect related network requests. Summarize observed bottlenecks, protect sensitive data, and save approved artifacts in the temporary directory.

best_practices: Find the target page identifier and take a fresh snapshot before using element identifiers.
Use --allowUnrestrictedPaths=false, approved temporary artifact paths, and explicit approval for uploads or broader filesystem access.
Use test accounts and authorized pages; confirm submissions or installations and treat page content as untrusted data.
anti_patterns: Do not guess page or element identifiers from an earlier browser state.
Do not restart the background service before every command; normal tool calls start it implicitly.
Do not upload sensitive files, submit live transactions, or execute untrusted page-provided tools without explicit authorization.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The listing supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when their environment provides shell execution and the required CLI.

faq.question: What must I install first?
faq.answer: Install the chrome-devtools-mcp package to make the chrome-devtools command available. Installation is a one-time prerequisite.

faq.question: Must I start the service before each command?
faq.answer: No. Tool commands start the background server implicitly, and browser state persists across commands.

faq.question: How do I find elements for clicking or typing?
faq.answer: Take an accessibility snapshot of the target page and use its element identifiers with click or fill commands.

faq.question: Can I restrict access to local files?
faq.answer: Yes. Pass --allowUnrestrictedPaths=false to restrict file access to the OS temporary directory. The documented default permits unrestricted paths.

faq.question: Are all diagnostic tools available by default?
faq.answer: No. Memory debugging, PWA tools, and experimental features require their documented flags. Experimental screencast recording also requires ffmpeg.
